track: C — command palette and renderer render hygiene

sections.summary: The palette no longer goes through lazy()/Suspense, so the first Cmd+P cannot pay React's 300 ms fallback throttle. CommandPalette.tsx now exports a plain CommandPalette panel that is open while mounted (the ref-driven CommandPaletteController is gone), commandPaletteModule.ts is a useSyncExternalStore module store shaped exactly like workspaceBoot.ts, and boot.tsx starts the chunk with `void loadCommandPalette()` right after createRoot().render(). A new always-mounted CommandPaletteHost owns visibility and the CommandPaletteHandle; until the module store resolves it renders CommandPaletteShell — a dialog with a focused input that imports nothing from CommandPalette.tsx — and the real panel then adopts the shell's text through a new `initialQuery` prop. App.tsx lost lazy(), Suspense, preloadCommandPalette, useCommandPaletteLoader, the requestIdleCallback warm effect and the Meta-key warm; a 12-line useCommandPaletteControls() replaced them, and the palette ref no longer flows into the workspace subtree.
sections.gates: bun run lint (clean); bun run typecheck (clean, after one 45 s wait for a transient error in Track D's src/main/index.ts); bun test CommandPalette.dom CommandPaletteHost.dom boot.dom App.dom useRepositorySearch -> 14 pass / 0 fail
sections.deviations: The plan said to render `module.CommandPaletteController`. Keeping a second ref-driven controller inside the chunk would duplicate the host's job, so the chunk exports the panel and the host is the single owner of open/closed. Same observable behaviour. The palette chunk (20,458 B) is confirmed absent from the boot chunk's source map.

sections.summary: useRepositorySearch moved out of AppLayout and into the palette, so a keystroke re-renders the palette and nothing else. Settled results reach the diff viewer through a new searchResultsStore module store (frozen EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS, identity bail-out on publish, cleared when the palette closes); DiffSurface reads it with useSyncExternalStore. Every content reset now goes through one shared frozen array instead of a fresh [] twice per query, and cancelContentSearch fires only when a request is actually outstanding. A new workspaceRenderMetric module wraps the existing reviewMetrics counter and mirrors it onto window.__horusMetrics.workspaceRenders, which is the exact expression scripts/perf/startup-probe.mjs already reads.
sections.gates: bun run lint (clean); bun run typecheck (clean); bun test CommandPalette.dom CommandPaletteHost.dom useRepositorySearch searchResultsStore -> 16 pass / 0 fail
sections.deviations: DiffSurface keeps its `contentSearch` prop as an explicit override (`contentSearch ?? publishedSearch`) instead of dropping it. Removing it would require editing RepositoryWorkspace.tsx/WorkspaceRoot.tsx beyond the one-line render counter Track C owns, and typecheck would fail until someone else did it. Recorded as needs-owner. RepositoryWorkspace.tsx was touched only for `useEffect(markRepositoryWorkspaceRender)` -> `useEffect(markWorkspaceRender)` plus its import.

sections.summary: An empty query is now an offer rather than an empty filter. createFileSearchIndex derives every ancestor directory once per snapshot (single-slot cached on the path array identity) and entries carry `kind: 'file' | 'dir'`; rankFilePaths takes an options object and, for an empty query, returns a priority list built in one pass — recent files for this root in recency order, then changed/review paths, then top-level directories, then tree order, capped at 40. Directory rows render with IconFolder. Recents live in renderer localStorage keyed by root (max 20) behind a new useRecentFiles hook that keeps the root next to the list in state, so switching projects can never persist one history under the other's key; App.tsx's in-memory 10-entry list is gone. The palette puts Files above Commands for an empty query, collapses commands to three plus a "More commands…" row that switches the query to `>`, and shows ghost text for the top path-prefix match that Tab accepts.
sections.gates: bun run lint (clean); bun run lint:css (clean); bun run typecheck (clean); bun test over the 10 owned/affected files -> 60 pass / 0 fail
sections.deviations: Selecting a directory narrows the query to `<path>/` and keeps the palette open, instead of "expands and reveals it in the Explorer". The Explorer's expansion state lives inside RepositoryWorkspace/@pierre/trees, which Track C may not edit and which exposes no reveal API. Recorded as needs-owner for P27. Also added DIRECTORY_SCORE_PENALTY = 1 so a folder only outranks a file when no file matched nearly as well — without it `services/` beat `service.py` for the query "service".

sections.summary: Renderer half only. The fixed 240 ms debounce became 180/120/90 ms by query length (long from five characters up), paste still fires at once, and a path-like query — a `/` in it, or five or more file-name prefix hits — waits a full 400 ms before spending a ripgrep, paste included. countFileNameMatches in fileSearch computes the hit count over the <= 32 ranked results so RankedPath does not have to carry scores. useRepositorySearch keeps its pending dispatch in a ref and exposes flushContentSearch(); the palette calls it from Enter when there is nothing to open, so Enter resolves a deferred search instead of doing nothing.
sections.gates: bun run lint (clean); bun run lint:css (clean); bun run typecheck (clean); bun test contentSearchScheduler useRepositorySearch fileSearch CommandPalette.dom CommandPaletteHost.dom searchResultsStore -> 49 pass / 0 fail
sections.deviations: Two. (1) "Fire immediately on Enter" is limited to the case where Enter would otherwise do nothing; flushing on every Enter would spawn a ripgrep that the closing palette immediately cancels. (2) ">= 5 files with score above threshold" is implemented as ">= 5 file-name prefix hits" — RankedPath carries no score, and a raw match count would make nearly every three-letter query path-like. Did not touch src/main (Track D owns MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS).

sections.summary: The palette's backdrop blur drops from 30px to 12px, the panel gets `contain: layout paint`, and `will-change: transform, opacity` is applied only through a `data-opening` attribute that CommandPalette clears 80 ms after mount (matching --duration-instant, the scrim fade), so no compositor layer is pinned for the life of the palette.

sections.deviations: The blur change goes through an inherited `--surface-blur` custom property set on .command-palette-layer rather than a separate .command-palette rule: splitting the shared `.command-palette, .pr-loading-indicator` selector list tripped stylelint no-duplicate-selectors, and .pr-loading-indicator is not Track C's to change. The CDP frame-timing verification needs an installed build and was not run here.

sections.summary: The React Compiler now compiles every hot component. Three causes were isolated by bisecting a scratch copy against the plugin's own logger: refs read into an object literal during render (the `view` object carried commandPaletteRef and terminalDockRef, and AppLayout read view.terminalDockRef — both refs now travel as their own JSX props and neither reaches the workspace subtree); try/finally in the three folder-open handlers, which the compiler cannot lower; and the eager `initialWorkspacePaint(...)` plus `firstOpenPathForSnapshot(...)` in App's body, now `useState(() => …)`. That last one also cleared 13 PreserveManualMemo errors, so no manual memoisation had to be deleted. CommandPalette's row className used `[a, b].filter(Boolean).join(' ') || undefined`, a logical test over a ternary chain the compiler rejects; it is now a small lookup function. electron.vite.config.ts wires the plugin's `logger` behind HORUS_COMPILER_LOG=1.
sections.gates: bun run lint (clean); bun run lint:css (clean); bun run typecheck (clean); bun test reactCompiler CommandPalette.dom CommandPaletteHost.dom App.dom boot.dom recentFiles.dom -> 29 pass / 0 fail. Before: App/AppLayout/AgentSessionLayout all CompileError (refs, try-finally), CommandPalette CompileError (ternary). After: CompileSuccess for App, AppLayout, AgentSessionLayout, CachedWorkspaceFallback, CommandPalette, SearchPreview, CommandPaletteHost, CommandPaletteShell, RepositoryWorkspace.
sections.deviations: No dom test for the boot-paint change: rendering App under bun needs stubs for ~12 IPC methods plus useGitWorkflow/useAgentSession and there is no existing App render test to build on. `useState(() => …)` moves when pure work runs, not what it returns, and the new reactCompiler.test.ts covers the part that can silently regress. RepositoryWorkspace.tsx still has one other component (around line 985) that bails on ref access — outside Track C's ownership, left for P13/Track E.

sections.summary: Per-row closures are gone from the results list. Rows carry data-index and one delegated onPointerMove on the list resolves the row with closest('[data-index]'), setting state only when the index changes; the per-row ref callback and the rowRefs array went with it (keyboard scroll-into-view now uses resultsRef.querySelector). Row models are memoised on results identity via a groups memo that carries each section's starting index, so no `let rowIndex` is mutated across nested map callbacks. rankFilePaths keeps a single-slot cache of its arguments and result and hands back the previous array when a recomputation is element-wise identical, so one more typed character usually costs zero row rebuilds.

sections.deviations: None. The groups memo had to be written as a for loop rather than a map with an outer accumulator — reassigning a captured variable inside a callback is "Cannot reassign variable after render completes" to the compiler, which reactCompiler.test.ts caught immediately.

gateSummary: Final run, all green. `bun run lint` -> oxlint clean, no warnings. `bun run lint:css` -> stylelint clean. `bun run typecheck` -> tsc -b clean. `bun test src/renderer` -> 574 pass / 0 fail across 96 files (6.4 s). `bun test src/shared` -> 73 pass / 0 fail across 9 files. Targeted re-run of the 15 files covering everything Track C touched -> 95 pass / 0 fail. `bun run build` -> exit 0 (only the pre-existing "chunks larger than 500 kB" advisory). `bun run check:entry` -> exit 0: pre-mount closure 1,652,713 B across 20 chunks (limit 1,700,000; Wave 1 left it at 1,649,485 B, so +3,228 B), boot chunk boot-mooE_MZK.js 174,866 B (Wave 1 left it at 172,134 B, so +2,732 B), entry closure 2,935 B (limit 65,536), WorkerPool absent from the boot chunk. Boot-chunk composition verified from the source map: Welcome.tsx and CommandPalette.tsx are out (own chunks of 5,233 B and 20,458 B; the palette chunk also carries useRepositorySearch, fileSearch, contentSearchScheduler and searchPreview), searchResultsStore landed in the DiffSurface-shared chunk, CommandPaletteHost stayed in boot by design. The +2.7 KB is the React Compiler's memoisation for App, AppLayout, AgentSessionLayout and CachedWorkspaceFallback — all four were skipped before P19 and emitted no cache code at all — plus the palette host, module store, recentFiles and workspaceRenderMetric. Typecheck failed transiently twice on files owned by other tracks (src/main/index.ts `preferredRoots`, src/shared/sessionRestore.test.ts `pendingPullRequestUrl`); both were green on retry after waiting, and neither was touched. No probe numbers were measured: startup-probe `palette.openMs` / `emptyRows` / `contentResultsMs` / `workspaceRenders` and the CDP frame timing all need the installed build, which is the reviewer's step.
reviewNotes:
Risky spots, decisions and things I could not verify.

1. P17 spawn trade-off, worth a second opinion. At roughly 90 ms per character the new 90 ms bucket starts one ripgrep per keystroke, each cancelling the last (`cancelContentSearch` now fires only when one is genuinely outstanding). At 60 ms per character it still coalesces to a single search. This is what the plan asks for and it depends on Track D's main half (MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS 24, capped threads, kill on cap) to stay cheap. If the shim shows a spawn storm, raise CONTENT_SEARCH_LONG_QUERY_MS in contentSearchScheduler.ts — it is one constant.

2. DiffSurface's `contentSearch` prop is now dead weight. Nothing supplies it: App stopped passing it, but RepositoryWorkspace.tsx (lines ~217, ~641, ~847, ~946, ~1290, ~1527) and WorkspaceRoot still thread it, and Track C may not edit those. DiffSurface reads `contentSearch ?? publishedSearch`. Whoever owns RepositoryWorkspace next (Track E, P27) should delete the prop from RepositoryWorkspaceProps/WorkspaceViewerProps and both DiffSurface call sites, then drop it from DiffSurfaceProps and the `??`.

3. Palette directory rows do not reveal in the Explorer. Selecting a folder narrows the query to `<path>/` and keeps the palette open. Expansion state lives inside RepositoryWorkspace/@pierre/trees with no reveal API; doing it properly needs a `revealPath` on RepositoryWorkspace that App forwards to CommandPaletteHost. Natural fit for P27.

4. package.json needs `@babel/core` in devDependencies. reactCompiler.test.ts imports it and it currently resolves only as a transitive dependency of @vitejs/plugin-react. It works today; it is one hoisting change away from a confusing failure. Not in Track C's ownership, so not done.

5. reactCompiler.test.ts is the load-bearing new gate. A component the compiler skips emits no memoisation and the build says nothing about it — that is exactly how App, AppLayout and AgentSessionLayout ended up unmemoised. The test runs babel + babel-plugin-react-compiler over four files (~1.2 s) and fails with the reported reasons. It caught one regression during P20 (an accumulator reassigned inside `.map`). If Wave 3/4 add components to those files, add their names to HOT_COMPONENTS.

6. Test isolation caveat found the hard way. Running many dom files in one bun process made an early host assertion flaky: with ./CommandPalette already in bun's module registry, `import()` resolves inside the same `act()` and the real palette mounts on the first frame, so "the shell renders first" is not a stable property under `bun test`. The shell is now covered by rendering CommandPaletteShell directly, and the host test asserts the timing-independent property instead (an input is focused the moment `open()` returns, and whatever was typed survives into the palette). A second, related fix: a `screen.queryAllByRole('button')` assertion passed alone and failed in the full suite because another file had left a button in document.body — it is now scoped to the render container. Watch for that pattern in other tracks' new dom tests.

7. P18's `will-change` is a judgement call. The palette panel has no transform/opacity transition of its own — only the scrim fades — so `will-change: transform, opacity` is really a request to hold the panel on its own compositor layer through the opening frames rather than an animation hint. It is scoped to `[data-opening]` and dropped after 80 ms. The measurable part of P18 is the 30px -> 12px blur and `contain: layout paint`.

8. Could not verify anything that needs the installed build: palette.openMs <= 30 ms on the first Cmd+P, palette.emptyRows >= 20, palette.contentResultsMs <= 150, palette.workspaceRenders delta of 0 across six typed characters, and the CDP frame timing around Cmd+P. The renderer-side guarantee for the render count is covered by a dom test (a memo'd workspace stand-in calling markWorkspaceRender while six characters are typed into the palette), and window.__horusMetrics.workspaceRenders is now populated so the probe's existing expression works.

9. Two mechanical changes with wide reach, in case a bisect points here: `rankFilePaths` changed signature from `(paths, query, limit?, priorityPaths?)` to `(paths, query, options?)` and now returns `{ path, kind }[]` rather than `string[]`; and `App.tsx`'s three folder-open handlers moved their `finally` cleanup to after the try/catch (no `return` sits inside those try blocks, so this is equivalent).
